text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN AND CORN SALE - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group late on Thursday bought a combined shipment of 38,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn, traders said. Shipment was slated for November 10-25, U.S. Gulf and/or November 26-December 10, Pacific Northwest.
FLOUR SALE - Three Turkish millers have agreed with Libya to sell it 40,000 tonnes of wheat flour for November and December shipment, officials from the milling companies said on Thursday.

WHEAT TENDER - Moroccan millers group, Comite Professionnel de la Minoterie, passed up import tenders for 18,500 tonnes of soft wheat, saying prices offered were too high. The group was considering launching another tender soon but the spokesman gave no details. The original tender was for delivery in the second half of October.

Armenia will seek 21,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for up to November 20 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. The wheat would come from the European Community, Ukraine or, if U.S. origin, only hard red winter no.2. The latest date for offers was October 14, Yerevan, Armenia.
WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Slovenia was expected to tender early next week for 35,000 to 40,000 tonnes U.S. hard red spring wheat, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for October 12-November 15.
- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to place a tender within two weeks for two 34,000-tonne shipments of U.S. wheat, local traders said. No details were available.
- Sri Lanka on October 18 will seek 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat. It said 50,000 tonnes would be soft white wheat and 50,000 tonnes hard red winter wheat for November 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for November. October 1 was the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.

BARLEY TENDER - Cyprus will tender on Thursday for 25,000 tonnes optional origin feed barley, U.S. exporters said. Shipment was slated for October 15-30. "It will not be U.S. barley," one U.S. exporter said of prospective suppliers.

RICE TENDER - Sri Lanka will soon invite bids for 50,000 tonnes of rice for November/December delivery, officials of the state buying arm Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The new purchase will be for delivery in November and December and there will be no restrictions on rice origin.

MARKET TALK - China is heading for a record corn crop this year and will have plenty left over for export if the government lifts a long-term ban on selling the grain overseas, traders and diplomats said. The corn crop under harvest in the far northeast looks set to be between 115-120 million tonnes, said grain sources just returned from a tour of the region.

MARKET TALK - cont'd - Rumours that Egypt has cancelled a wheat shipment probably arose from routine delays to wheat or flour cargoes for health inspection, a trader said on Thursday. The Cairo-based trader, Wayne Bacon of Oriac International, said he thought some U.S. soft red winter wheat was on hold on suspicion it contained high levels of scab (fusarium). Some wheat flour, probably of French origin and bought by a private Alexandria company at $286 a tonne, was also on hold for similar reasons, he added. But an official at the state's General Authority for Supply Authority, the main Egyptian grain buyer, said he had no information on any cancellation of a wheat shipment.
... USDA offered six Andean nations a total of $350 million in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. farmgoods under the Export Crdit Guarantee Program (GSM-102) for fiscal 1997.
It also authorized $154 million in credit guarantees for sales of U.S. farm goods to South Korea under GSM 102.
